title: Fix post-archive no-active status diagnosis
outOfScope: Weakening no-active protection for arbitrary ungoverned worktree changes.
Changing immutable archive evidence or the archive writer transaction.
Implementing RFE-ISSUE-152 nested Make propagation or RFE-ISSUE-082 release reconciliation.

sources.reason: The validator and repair entrypoint that reproduce the impossible repair recommendation.
Existing no-active live-change and generator behavior regressions.
Existing archive transaction and start-receipt ownership regressions.
Immutable real evidence whose changedFiles list owns the complete post-archive, pre-commit diff.
Immutable manifest binding the real archived Contract and Summary.
Historical RFE-116 design that solved only matching start-receipt ownership and preserved unrelated fail-closed behavior.
Authoritative release-blocking process issue history including RFE-106 and RFE-116.

riskAssessment.reason: A broad exemption could hide ungoverned no-active edits, while the current contradiction makes the canonical post-archive state appear repairable when repair cannot change it.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized permanent process fixes before later Work Items and release, and no new product decision is required.

preReviewWarnings: Only a complete currently changed archive bundle may own post-archive pre-commit paths.
Archived Summary changedFiles must be used as the path ownership source; scope alone is insufficient.
Every unrelated, omitted, malformed, or historical-only path must remain fail closed.
repair-ai-status must not claim it can resolve ungoverned live changes.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: No-active consistency accepts the canonical post-ai-finish, pre-first-commit state only when every live path is owned by a complete currently changed archive transaction and its immutable archived Summary changedFiles.

A qualifying archive transaction requires the current index update, same-task Start Receipt, Contract, Summary, and valid manifest that binds the exact archive paths; historical files alone never qualify.
Any live path omitted from the archived Summary, any unrelated path, malformed Summary changedFiles, incomplete bundle, mismatched manifest, or orphan receipt remains fail closed.

The diagnostic distinguishes stale serialized Status from ungoverned live changes: only stale Status recommends repair; unowned dirt explicitly says repair cannot resolve it and directs the operator to restore changes or create/resume a Work Item.
repair-ai-status succeeds or is idempotent for a fully owned post-archive transaction and a clean no-active tree, but fails before rewriting Status for unowned live changes.
Existing one-active-pair repair, stale no-active refresh rollback, archive receipt ownership, and clean post-commit behavior remain unchanged.
English and Japanese Cockpit/status guidance describe the exact archive-owned exception and actionable failure paths without implying that any dirty no-active tree is acceptable.
Bidirectional traceability records the RFE-153 extension of RFE-106/RFE-116, its implementation, negative tests, and complete lifecycle.

Focused regressions, all Contract checks, full quality, archive, aggregate PR validation, Hosted CI, merge, ai-close-work-item, branch cleanup, and synchronized clean main complete before RFE-152 starts.
guidelines: Use systematic root-cause debugging and red-green-refactor TDD; do not patch the generated Status marker to hide live changes.
Derive post-archive ownership from the valid manifest-bound archived Summary changedFiles, not from broad path prefixes or Contract scope alone.
Keep arbitrary no-active live changes fail closed and emit remediation that the named command can actually perform.
Preserve byte-for-byte Status on a failed repair attempt.
Keep English and Japanese lifecycle semantics aligned.

intent.problem: After RFE-151 ai-finish, check-ai-status-consistency rejected the canonical no-active post-archive pre-commit worktree and recommended repair-ai-status. The generator intentionally writes a deterministic zero-change marker, so repair regenerated the same bytes and failed again. RFE-116 only excluded the matching Start Receipt; implementation and documentation paths listed by the archived Summary remain misclassified.
constraints: The complete archive transaction must remain immutable and must be the only source of temporary ownership.
No arbitrary dirty no-active worktree may pass.
The fix must preserve clean post-commit validation and active-pair repair behavior.
Release and later process Work Items remain blocked until this corrective completes its full lifecycle.
intent.rationale: Classify the entire current change set against a valid changed archive bundle and its archived Summary changedFiles. This makes the canonical archive-before-commit transition machine-verifiable while keeping any unowned path fail closed and replacing impossible repair advice with truthful recovery.

rawUserRequest: Complete all release-blocking Work Items through full lifecycle, and when a process issue is found, fix the process before continuing so the error cannot recur. During RFE-151 closure, check-ai-status-consistency rejected the post-ai-finish, pre-first-commit state and instructed repair-ai-status; repair reproduced the same failure. Root cause investigation proved the no-active generator intentionally records zero transient changes while the checker treats the governed archived implementation diff as unowned. Fix this permanently before RFE-152, RFE-ISSUE-082, Japanese assessment, documentation alignment, cleanup, and release.

declaredIntent.summary: Make post-archive no-active ownership and repair diagnostics truthful without weakening fail-closed governance.

scenarioCoverage.expected: No-active consistency and repair accept the governed pre-first-commit transition without serializing transient paths.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add a red-first fixture with implementation, docs, Start Receipt, archive pair, manifest, index, and matching Summary changedFiles.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The same bundle has one unrelated or Summary-omitted live path.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Validation fails closed with an explicit message that repair cannot resolve ownership and leaves Status unchanged.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add negative fixtures for unrelated source and path omitted from changedFiles, then assert repair performs no generator subprocess.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The archive bundle is incomplete, historical-only, malformed, or manifest-mismatched.
scenarioCoverage.expected: No transaction ownership is granted and every live path remains visible.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Extend existing RFE-116 fixtures with malformed Summary changedFiles and mismatched/current-versus-historical bundle cases.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The persisted no-active Status itself contains stale changed files or a nonzero count.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Validation recommends repair and repair regenerates a deterministic no-active marker.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Preserve and strengthen the existing serialized-status repair regression.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The archive bundle has been committed and the no-active worktree is clean.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Consistency passes with no transaction exception and no stale diagnostic.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run a clean fixture and the real post-commit repository check.
